assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope is the creative novelty and derivative-risk-flagging method; legal sufficiency (fair use, substantial similarity, licensing) is delegated to compliance_heavy (FP6/KU8)
a source inventory and a history of the system's own prior outputs are available to compute distances
transformation and added original elements raise novelty and lower near-copy probability but never constitute a legal safe harbor
exclusions: legal-sufficiency, fair-use, and substantial-similarity determinations (delegated to compliance_heavy, scope FP6/KU8)
aesthetic quality grading and editorial taste judgments
platform distribution scheduling and paid media

competency_questions.question: What is the operating definition of an original output, and why is novelty alone insufficient?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORIGINALITY_DEFINITION fixes originality as novel AND appropriate

competency_questions.question: How are the source materials an output draws on identified so borrowing can be measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_INVENTORY enumerates concrete sources and their roles

competency_questions.question: How is novelty generated by recombining known elements and exploring within a style space (Boden's combinational/exploratory modes)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMBINATIONAL_CREATIVITY and EXPLORATORY_CREATIVITY define recombination and within-space exploration

competency_questions.question: What is transformational creativity and how does it differ from exploring within a space?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSFORMATIONAL_CREATIVITY alters a space-defining constraint, unlike EXPLORATORY_CREATIVITY

competency_questions.question: What is the modify-and-add directive, how does it lower near-copy probability, and what counts as a verified added own element?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSFORM_NOT_COPY requires measurable departure; ADD_OWN_ELEMENT verifies a distinguishing original contribution

competency_questions.question: How is reusable style separated from protectable expression, and how does pastiche differ from parody?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STYLE_VS_EXPRESSION flags the boundary; PASTICHE_VS_PARODY classifies imitation versus commentary

competency_questions.question: How is distance from external sources and from the system's own prior outputs measured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_DISTANCE and PRIOR_OUTPUT_DISTANCE compute the two distance signals

competency_questions.question: How are the two distances combined into a novelty score gated by appropriateness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NOVELTY_SCORE combines source and prior distances under an appropriateness gate

competency_questions.question: How is the novelty-versus-appropriateness tradeoff set per brief so neither reckless novelty nor defensive sameness dominates?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NOVELTY_APPROPRIATENESS_BALANCE picks the per-brief operating point against the originality definition

competency_questions.question: How is overuse of the same device prevented and how is format wear-out anticipated before fatigue?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPETITION_GUARD enforces cooldowns; FRESHNESS_DECAY models format decay and retire-or-refresh

competency_questions.question: How are near-copy passages detected and surfaced as evidence rather than as verdicts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE surfaces low-distance spans as evidence

competency_questions.question: How is derivative risk flagged, and why is transformation explicitly NOT treated as a legal safe harbor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DERIVATIVE_RISK_FLAG raises a non-safe-harbor flag asserting elevated risk and the need for legal screening

competency_questions.question: How is borrowed material attributed and how is legal sufficiency routed out of this KB to compliance_heavy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_ATTRIBUTION records provenance; COMPLIANCE_ROUTING routes legal-sufficiency decisions to compliance_heavy

competency_questions.question: How is every novelty and derivative-risk decision made reconstructable and auditable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NOVELTY_AUDIT_TRAIL records the full decision provenance

glossary.definition: the property of being both novel (different from prior work) and appropriate (fitting the brief/context); per the standard definition of creativity
novelty produced by unfamiliar combinations of familiar elements (Boden)
novelty produced by exploring unfilled regions of an accepted conceptual space without breaking its rules (Boden)
novelty produced by altering a defining constraint of the conceptual space itself (Boden)
the principle that ideas/styles/methods are reusable while a source's specific fixed expression is protectable
non-satirical imitation of a style with no commentary on a specific target (Genette)
transformation of a specific target that comments on or subverts it (Genette)
the estimated likelihood that an output reproduces protectable expression of a source closely enough to require legal screening
a legal protection that clears a use; explicitly NOT something transformation provides and NOT decided in this KB
the loss of perceived novelty of a format/device over time and exposure as it wears out

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for novelty and derivative-risk work units, informed by Boden's three modes of creativity, Lessig's remix economy, Genette's pastiche/parody distinction, and the standard (novelty-plus-appropriateness) definition of creativity; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Boden 1990/2004 The Creative Mind: Myths and Mechanisms (combinational, exploratory, transformational creativity); Lessig 2008 Remix: Making Art and Commerce Thrive in the Hybrid Economy; Genette 1982 Palimpsestes (pastiche vs parody); Runco & Jaeger 2012 The Standard Definition of Creativity, Creativity Research Journal 24(1):92-96

nodes.definition: Fix the operating definition of an original output as BOTH novel (different from what exists) AND appropriate (fitting the brief/audience/context); neither half alone qualifies. This is the yardstick every downstream novelty judgment is measured against.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: definition of originality or appropriateness criterion revised

pros.claim: A two-pronged definition stops 'random = creative': a novel but off-brief output is rejected, not praised
pros.example: a surreal tagline that ignores the product is novel but inappropriate, so not original

cons.claim: Appropriateness is context-relative, so the same output can be original in one brief and derivative in another
cons.example: reusing a meme format is fresh for a niche but stale for a mainstream audience

failure_modes: scoring novelty alone and calling it creativity
conflating 'appropriate' with 'safe/legal'
acceptance_tests: every novelty judgment cites both a novelty term and an appropriateness term
revisit_triggers: originality definition revised
appropriateness rubric for a new brief class added

nodes.definition: Enumerate the concrete source materials the output draws on (referenced works, prompts, exemplars, style targets) so that borrowing can be measured and attributed rather than assumed absent.

included: per-source role (style target vs content source)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new source class (e.g. live web retrieval) enters the pipeline

pros.claim: Naming sources up front turns 'is this derivative?' from a guess into a measurable distance from named items
pros.example: listing the one viral post a draft was 'inspired by' lets distance be computed against it

cons.claim: Hidden or laundered sources (style absorbed via training) may never appear in the inventory
cons.example: an output copies a living artist's signature style with no explicit source reference

failure_modes: unlisted source that the output actually copies
treating absence-of-citation as absence-of-borrowing
acceptance_tests: every claimed-original output has an explicit (possibly empty, justified) source inventory
revisit_triggers: new source channel added
an uninventoried source surfaces in review

nodes.definition: Boden's first creativity mode: generate novelty by making unfamiliar combinations of familiar elements (concepts, references, formats), where each element is known but the juxtaposition is not.

excluded: inventing genuinely new primitive elements (that is transformational, not combinational)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the combination-space or element vocabulary changes

pros.claim: Recombination is the highest-yield, lowest-risk novelty lever: known parts, new whole, low copy risk per part
pros.example: pairing a noir voiceover with a cooking tutorial is novel yet copies neither source wholesale

cons.claim: A combination can still be a near-copy if one element dominates and is itself protected expression
cons.example: 'recombining' is a fig leaf if 95% is one source plus a trivial tweak

failure_modes: combination dominated by a single source element
arbitrary mash-up that is novel but inappropriate
acceptance_tests: the output recombines >=2 distinct elements with no single element exceeding a dominance threshold
revisit_triggers: element vocabulary expanded
combinations observed to collapse onto one source

nodes.definition: Boden's second mode: generate novelty by exploring the unfilled regions of an accepted conceptual/stylistic space (a genre, a format, a brand system) without breaking its rules.

included: search of unfilled regions in a fixed space

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the bounded style space or its rules change

pros.claim: Exploration yields on-brand novelty: new instances that obey the brand rules, maximizing appropriateness
pros.example: a new ad in an established campaign that fans recognize yet have not seen

cons.claim: Exhaustive exploration of a small space hits diminishing novelty fast as regions fill up
cons.example: the tenth variation on the same format reads as a rerun

failure_modes: mistaking exploration for transformation (the rules were never broken)
over-exploring a near-exhausted space
acceptance_tests: new instances stay inside the declared style rules while differing from prior instances in the space
revisit_triggers: style space redefined
novelty yield per new instance drops below threshold

nodes.definition: Boden's third and rarest mode: generate novelty by altering or dropping a defining constraint of the space itself, producing outputs the unmodified space could not contain.

included: creating outputs the old space could not hold

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the set of space-defining constraints is reconsidered

pros.claim: Transformation produces the most defensible, highest-novelty outputs because the result is structurally unlike the source
pros.example: removing the 'single narrator' rule of a format opens an output class no prior instance occupies

cons.claim: Transformation is high-risk and often inappropriate: breaking the rule can also break the brief or audience fit
cons.example: dropping a brand's core constraint yields novelty the brand cannot use

failure_modes: breaking a constraint that was load-bearing for appropriateness
claiming transformation while merely re-skinning a copy
acceptance_tests: a named space-defining constraint is explicitly altered/dropped and the result is verified appropriate to the brief
revisit_triggers: space-defining constraint set changes
a transformation breaks audience fit in testing

nodes.definition: The core operating directive: do not reproduce a source; instead modify it and add an own element so the output is structurally and expressively distinct. This raises novelty and lowers near-copy probability, but is a CREATIVE measure, not a legal guarantee.

included: modify the source rather than reproduce it
excluded: asserting legal sufficiency of the transformation (delegated to compliance_heavy)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the transform/add directive or its measurable thresholds change

pros.claim: Modify-and-add is the single highest-leverage move for both novelty and copy-risk reduction
pros.example: rewriting a borrowed structure and inserting an original framing device departs measurably from the source

cons.claim: Transformation degree is a spectrum, and a small tweak to heavily-copied expression is still a near-copy that this lever cannot launder
cons.example: find-and-replace on a protected text 'modifies' it but remains a copy

failure_modes: treating any modification as sufficient
adding a cosmetic element while the core remains copied
acceptance_tests: the output measurably departs from every inventoried source on structure AND expression, with the departure logged
revisit_triggers: transform thresholds revised
a 'transformed' output later flagged as a near-copy

nodes.definition: Isolate and require at least one genuinely original contributed element (a framing, a juxtaposition, a new component) that no source supplied; this is the distinguishing creative lever that converts borrowing into authorship.

included: identification of the added original element

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the bar for what counts as an own element changes

pros.claim: Naming the specific added element makes 'we contributed something' auditable, not rhetorical
pros.example: the log records exactly which framing device the author invented versus inherited

cons.claim: An added element can be original yet trivial, leaving the substantive content still derivative
cons.example: an original title bolted onto an otherwise copied body adds little distinguishing weight

failure_modes: adding an element that is original but immaterial to the whole
claiming an added element that is itself borrowed
acceptance_tests: at least one named element is verified present in the output and absent from every inventoried source
revisit_triggers: own-element bar revised
an 'added element' found to be itself derivative

nodes.definition: Apply the idea/expression distinction operationally: general ideas, styles, genres, and methods are reusable creative raw material, while a source's specific, fixed expression is the protectable thing not to reproduce. Flag, do not adjudicate, the boundary.

excluded: the legal idea/expression determination itself (delegated to compliance_heavy)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the operational idea/expression boundary heuristics change

pros.claim: Separating reusable style from protectable expression lets the system borrow boldly at the idea level while guarding the expression level
pros.example: emulating a noir STYLE is fine; reproducing a specific noir SCRIPT's lines is flagged

cons.claim: The idea/expression line is genuinely blurry and fact-specific; the system can only approximate and must defer the hard cases
cons.example: whether a distinctive plot structure is 'idea' or 'expression' is contestable

failure_modes: copying specific expression while believing only 'style' was borrowed
treating the heuristic boundary as a legal ruling
acceptance_tests: each borrowing is classified as idea/style-layer (reusable) or expression-layer (flag-for-review), with rationale
revisit_triggers: idea/expression heuristics change
a 'style-only' borrow later judged to copy expression

nodes.definition: Genette's distinction: classify the output's relation to a target as pastiche (non-satirical imitation of a style, no commentary) versus parody (transformation of a specific target that comments on it). The relation changes both creative intent and the risk profile.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the pastiche/parody taxonomy or target-identification rule changes

pros.claim: Distinguishing imitation from commentary clarifies intent and routes risk: parody transforms a target, pastiche merely wears its style
pros.example: a video that mocks a specific ad is parody-with-commentary; a generic 'in the style of' clip is pastiche

cons.claim: Pastiche imitation can shade into copying a recognizable expression, and parody's protection is jurisdiction-specific and not decidable here
cons.example: an 'homage' pastiche that reproduces a signature sequence is closer to copying than to commentary

failure_modes: labeling a copy as 'parody' to imply safety
pastiche that imitates protectable expression, not just style
acceptance_tests: the output is labeled pastiche or parody (or neither) with its target and commentary status recorded
revisit_triggers: pastiche/parody taxonomy changes
a labeled 'parody' lacks any commentary on its target

nodes.definition: Estimate how far the candidate output sits from each inventoried source along structural and expressive axes; small distance to a protectable source is the primary derivative-risk signal.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the source-distance metric or its axes change

pros.claim: A per-source distance turns derivative risk into a continuous, rankable signal instead of a yes/no hunch
pros.example: the draft scores 0.2 distance from one source and 0.8 from another, pinpointing the risky one

cons.claim: Distance metrics are proxy measures; semantic copying can be lexically distant and a paraphrase can be semantically near
cons.example: a close paraphrase scores high lexical distance yet copies the underlying expression

failure_modes: over-trusting a single distance metric
distance computed against an incomplete source inventory
acceptance_tests: each inventoried source has a computed structural and expressive distance, with the nearest flagged
revisit_triggers: distance metric changes
a low-distance output passes without a derivative-risk flag

nodes.definition: Estimate how far the candidate sits from the system's OWN recent outputs; small distance to prior outputs signals self-repetition (recycling the same joke, hook, or format) rather than source-copying.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the prior-output window or self-similarity metric changes

pros.claim: Measuring distance from one's own history catches self-plagiarism and audience fatigue that source checks miss
pros.example: two posts a week apart reuse the same hook structure and are flagged as self-repetition

cons.claim: A consistent brand voice legitimately repeats motifs, so distance must distinguish signature from staleness
cons.example: a recurring catchphrase is on-brand repetition, not fatigue

failure_modes: flagging intentional brand motifs as repetition
window too short to catch a reused format from last month
acceptance_tests: the candidate's distance from each output in the recent window is computed and near-duplicates surfaced
revisit_triggers: prior-output window changes
a recycled format ships without being flagged

nodes.definition: Combine distance-from-source and distance-from-prior-outputs into a single novelty score, gated by appropriateness, so a high score means 'far from sources, far from our reruns, and still fitting the brief'.

included: appropriateness gate on the combined score
excluded: absolute creativity ranking across unrelated domains

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the novelty-score formula or appropriateness gate changes

pros.claim: One gated score makes novelty comparable across candidates and prevents 'novel but off-brief' from scoring high
pros.example: a candidate far from sources and reruns but off-brief is capped by the appropriateness gate

cons.claim: Collapsing two distances plus a gate into one number hides which term drove the result and can be gamed
cons.example: an output games the prior-output term by trivial surface changes while staying near a source

failure_modes: a high novelty score read as a low legal risk
the gate masking a near-copy that is merely brief-appropriate
acceptance_tests: the novelty score exposes its source-distance, prior-distance, and appropriateness sub-terms and is not reported as a legal signal
revisit_triggers: novelty formula changes
a high-novelty output is later flagged derivative

nodes.definition: Govern how often the same joke, hook, structure, or format may be reused across outputs, enforcing a cooldown so a successful device is not run into the ground.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the reuse cooldown policy or device taxonomy changes

pros.claim: A reuse governor converts the fuzzy 'don't overuse it' into an enforceable cooldown per device
pros.example: a hook used twice this week is blocked from a third use until its cooldown elapses

cons.claim: Cooldowns can suppress a device that is still resonating, trading freshness for lost performance
cons.example: retiring a format the audience still loves leaves engagement on the table

failure_modes: device taxonomy too coarse to count reuse
cooldown so strict it forbids a winning recurring bit
acceptance_tests: each reusable device has a reuse count and an enforced cooldown before it may repeat
revisit_triggers: cooldown policy changes
a device is overused despite the guard

nodes.definition: Model how a format, trend, or device loses novelty over time and exposure (it wears out), so the system retires or refreshes it before audience fatigue rather than after.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the decay model or trend-lifecycle data changes

pros.claim: Modeling decay lets the system anticipate staleness and refresh proactively instead of reacting to a flop
pros.example: a trend's decay curve flags it for retirement before its engagement collapses

cons.claim: Decay rates vary by audience and channel and are hard to estimate, risking premature retirement of evergreen formats
cons.example: an evergreen explainer format is wrongly retired on a generic decay curve

failure_modes: one global decay curve applied to heterogeneous formats
retiring an evergreen format as if it were a fad
acceptance_tests: each active format carries a freshness estimate and a retire-or-refresh trigger tied to a decay model
revisit_triggers: decay model recalibrated
a format flopped from fatigue before its decay flag fired

nodes.definition: Probe for the near-copy condition: passages or structures whose distance to a protectable source is below a low threshold, surfacing the specific overlapping spans as evidence rather than a verdict.

excluded: the legal substantial-similarity determination (delegated to compliance_heavy)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the near-copy threshold or span-matching method changes

pros.claim: Surfacing the exact overlapping spans gives compliance concrete evidence and gives authors a precise fix target
pros.example: the probe highlights the three sentences that closely track a source paragraph

cons.claim: Threshold choice trades false alarms against missed near-copies, and the probe cannot judge whether overlap is legally actionable
cons.example: a heavily-quoted-then-attributed passage trips the probe though it may be lawful

failure_modes: a low threshold buries authors in false alarms
probe output mistaken for a copyright determination
acceptance_tests: any region below the near-copy threshold is surfaced with its source, span, and distance as evidence (never as a verdict)
revisit_triggers: near-copy threshold changes
an actual near-copy passes the probe undetected

nodes.definition: Raise a derivative-risk flag whenever transformation may be insufficient, EXPLICITLY encoding that transformation is a creative measure and NOT a legal safe harbor; the flag asserts elevated risk and the need for legal screening, never that the output is clear.

included: risk flag with severity and reasons
excluded: deciding legal sufficiency, fair use, or licensing (delegated to compliance_heavy, scope FP6/KU8)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the derivative-risk flagging policy or safe-harbor stance changes

pros.claim: A flag that explicitly denies safe-harbor status prevents the dangerous inference 'we transformed it, so we are fine'
pros.example: the flag states: elevated derivative risk; transformation does not clear this; route to compliance

cons.claim: Over-flagging trains reviewers to ignore the flag, while under-flagging lets a near-copy ship as 'transformed'
cons.example: if every borrow is flagged critical, real risks get lost in the noise

failure_modes: treating the flag as a clearance once transformation is applied
suppressing the flag because an own element was added
acceptance_tests: any below-threshold or high-similarity output carries a derivative-risk flag stating it is NOT cleared and must be legally screened
the flag never asserts legal sufficiency under any transformation
revisit_triggers: safe-harbor policy or flag thresholds change
an output shipped on a 'transformed therefore safe' inference

nodes.definition: Maintain a per-output attribution record of what was borrowed, from which source, at the idea/style or expression layer, so provenance is available for both credit and compliance screening.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the attribution schema or credit policy changes

pros.claim: An attribution ledger makes borrowing transparent and feeds the derivative-risk flag and compliance with exact provenance
pros.example: the ledger shows which structure came from which source at which layer

cons.claim: Attribution records credit but does not create permission; an attributed borrow can still be a near-copy
cons.example: crediting a source does not make reproducing its expression lawful

failure_modes: treating attribution as permission
incomplete ledger missing a material borrow
acceptance_tests: every material borrow has a ledger entry naming source, layer, and the borrowed element
revisit_triggers: attribution schema changes
a material borrow ships without a ledger entry

nodes.definition: Resolve the standing tension between pushing novelty and preserving appropriateness/brief-fit, choosing the operating point per brief so neither maximal novelty nor maximal safety dominates by default.
outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the per-brief novelty/appropriateness operating point changes

pros.claim: Choosing the operating point explicitly stops the default from silently maximizing one axis at the other's expense
pros.example: a conservative brand brief weights appropriateness higher; an experimental brief weights novelty higher

cons.claim: The right operating point is brief- and risk-dependent and can be set wrong, over- or under-shooting novelty
cons.example: a conservative brief pushed to maximal novelty produces off-brand work

failure_modes: maximizing novelty regardless of brief
defaulting to safe sameness to avoid any risk
acceptance_tests: each brief records an explicit novelty/appropriateness operating point with a rationale, and outputs are scored against it
revisit_triggers: brief operating point changes
outputs cluster at one axis extreme against the brief

nodes.definition: Route every derivative-risk flag and its provenance to the compliance_heavy track (scope FP6 / KU8) for the legal-sufficiency determination, enforcing that this KB never decides fair use, substantial similarity, or licensing itself.

included: handoff package (flag + provenance + spans) to compliance_heavy
excluded: interpreting licenses or fair-use factors in this KB

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the compliance interface contract or scope boundary changes

pros.claim: A hard route to compliance_heavy makes the safe-harbor boundary a structural fact, not a hope: legal calls happen only there
pros.example: every flagged output is blocked from publish until compliance_heavy returns a determination

cons.claim: A heavy compliance gate adds latency and can bottleneck throughput if flagging is noisy
cons.example: an over-flagging upstream stage floods compliance and stalls the pipeline

failure_modes: bypassing the route when timelines are tight
deciding legal sufficiency upstream to 'save time'
acceptance_tests: every derivative-risk-flagged output is routed to compliance_heavy with full provenance and is blocked from finalization until that track returns a determination
no legal-sufficiency call is made within this KB
revisit_triggers: compliance interface changes
a flagged output published without a compliance determination

nodes.definition: Record the full provenance of every novelty decision: source inventory, distances, applied transformations, added elements, flags raised, and routing, so any novelty or derivative-risk judgment can be reconstructed and audited.

included: linkage of score, flag, and routing
excluded: compliance's own internal record (owned by that track)

outputs: novelty score with derivative-risk flag and provenance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the audit-trail schema or retention policy changes

pros.claim: A complete audit trail makes every novelty and risk call defensible and lets a flagged decision be reconstructed end to end
pros.example: an auditor can replay why an output scored high novelty yet was still flagged and routed

cons.claim: Full provenance adds storage and write overhead proportional to output volume
cons.example: logging every distance and transform for high-volume generation is costly

failure_modes: missing provenance prevents reconstructing a flag
trail volume overwhelms retention budget
acceptance_tests: every novelty/derivative decision carries a reconstructable trail of inventory, distances, transforms, flags, and routing
revisit_triggers: audit schema changes
a flagged decision could not be reconstructed from the trail

edges.why_related: reuse cooldowns and format decay jointly govern when a device must be retired
adding a genuine own element increases the candidate's distance from sources
a pastiche imitating protectable expression elevates the derivative-risk flag
the audit trail consumes and links the attribution ledger entries
the transform-and-add lever is creative, but treating it as a legal safe harbor directly conflicts with the obligation to flag derivative risk
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades output quality or compliance posture
edges.resolution_rule: transformation raises novelty but NEVER clears derivative risk: apply the transform lever for creativity, yet always let DERIVATIVE_RISK_FLAG fire on low source-distance and route to compliance_heavy regardless of how much was modified

edges.why_related: maximizing the novelty score conflicts with preserving appropriateness and brief-fit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades output quality or compliance posture
edges.resolution_rule: cap the novelty score by the brief's appropriateness gate: pursue novelty only up to the operating point set per brief, never maximizing novelty at the expense of fit

edges.why_related: an aggressive recombination can still embed a near-copy of one dominant source element
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades output quality or compliance posture
edges.resolution_rule: recombine boldly but verify per-element dominance: if any single recombined element falls below the near-copy threshold against a protectable source, the probe overrides the 'it is a new combination' claim

edges.why_related: a strict reuse cooldown can suppress an on-brand recurring motif that freshness decay would still consider fresh
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged tension degrades output quality or compliance posture
edges.resolution_rule: distinguish signature from staleness: exempt declared brand motifs from the reuse cooldown while still applying freshness decay to non-signature devices

conflict_axes.name: transformation_as_lever_vs_as_safe_harbor
conflict_axes.description: Transformation reliably raises novelty and lowers near-copy probability, but treating it as a legal clearance is the central error this KB exists to prevent; legal sufficiency belongs to compliance_heavy.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always flag and route despite transformation; never infer safe-harbor from modification

conflict_axes.name: novelty_maximization_vs_appropriateness
conflict_axes.description: Pushing novelty can erode brief-fit; defending appropriateness can collapse into safe sameness. The standard definition requires both.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set an explicit per-brief operating point; gate novelty by appropriateness

conflict_axes.name: recombination_boldness_vs_element_dominance
conflict_axes.description: Bold recombination yields novelty, but a single dominant protectable element turns the 'new combination' into a near-copy.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap per-element dominance and run the similarity probe on each element

conflict_axes.name: style_reuse_vs_expression_copying
conflict_axes.description: Reusing a style is legitimate raw material; reproducing specific protectable expression is the line, but the boundary is blurry and must be flagged, not adjudicated here.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: classify the borrow layer; flag expression-layer borrows for review

conflict_axes.name: signature_repetition_vs_freshness
conflict_axes.description: On-brand recurring motifs build recognition, but the same device overused causes fatigue; signature and staleness must be told apart.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: exempt declared signatures from cooldown; apply decay to the rest

conflict_axes.name: source_distance_vs_self_distance
conflict_axes.description: An output can be far from external sources yet a rerun of the system's own prior work, or vice versa; both distances matter and can disagree.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: score both distances separately and surface whichever is small

conflict_axes.name: flag_sensitivity_vs_alert_fatigue
conflict_axes.description: A sensitive derivative-risk flag catches near-copies but over-flagging trains reviewers to ignore it; threshold choice trades the two.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: calibrate the threshold and report severity, not a binary alarm

conflict_axes.name: pastiche_homage_vs_imitation_copying
conflict_axes.description: Pastiche/homage celebrates a style, but imitation can slide into reproducing a recognizable protectable sequence.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label pastiche vs parody and flag homages that reproduce specific expression

conflict_axes.name: provenance_completeness_vs_overhead
conflict_axes.description: A complete audit trail makes every novelty/risk call defensible but costs storage proportional to output volume.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: log decisions, distances, flags, and routing; sample verbose intermediates

edge_cases.description: An output is heavily copied from one source, then trivially modified, and shipped on the inference that 'we transformed it, so it is safe'.
edge_cases.trigger: transformation treated as a legal safe harbor instead of a creative lever
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the derivative-risk flag on low source-distance regardless of modification and route to compliance_heavy; the flag explicitly denies safe-harbor status

edge_cases.description: A near-copy of a protectable source passes because the source was never listed in the inventory.
edge_cases.trigger: an uninventoried source the output actually copies
edge_cases.mitigation: require an explicit (justified) source inventory; treat absence of citation as a risk, not as absence of borrowing

edge_cases.description: A 'new combination' is dominated by one protectable element and is effectively a copy of that element.
edge_cases.trigger: recombination where a single source element exceeds the dominance threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: cap per-element dominance and run the similarity probe on each recombined element

edge_cases.description: An output scores high novelty but is off-brief, and the high score is read as success.
edge_cases.trigger: novelty maximized without the appropriateness gate
edge_cases.mitigation: gate the novelty score by the per-brief appropriateness operating point

edge_cases.description: A close paraphrase copies the underlying expression but scores high lexical distance and evades the probe.
edge_cases.trigger: semantic copying that is lexically distant
edge_cases.mitigation: use both structural and expressive distance axes; do not rely on a single lexical metric

edge_cases.description: The same hook or format is reused too often and the audience tunes out.
edge_cases.trigger: a successful device run past its cooldown and decay threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce per-device cooldowns and retire-or-refresh formats on the decay model

edge_cases.description: An evergreen format is wrongly retired because a generic decay curve was applied.
edge_cases.trigger: one global decay curve applied to a heterogeneous format
edge_cases.mitigation: calibrate decay per format/audience; exempt verified evergreen formats

edge_cases.description: A pastiche 'homage' reproduces a recognizable protectable sequence and is labeled safe as 'just style'.
edge_cases.trigger: pastiche that imitates protectable expression rather than only style
edge_cases.mitigation: classify the borrow layer; flag expression-layer imitation even when labeled homage

edge_cases.description: A material borrow is attributed (credited) and then assumed cleared because credit was given.
edge_cases.mitigation: keep attribution and clearance separate; route attributed near-copies to compliance anyway

edge_cases.description: A flagged output is published anyway because the compliance route was bypassed under deadline pressure.
edge_cases.trigger: compliance routing skipped to save time
edge_cases.mitigation: hard-block finalization of any flagged output until compliance_heavy returns a determination

edge_cases.description: A derivative-risk decision cannot be reconstructed later because provenance was not logged.
edge_cases.trigger: audit trail not recorded for a novelty/risk decision
edge_cases.mitigation: record inventory, distances, transforms, flags, and routing for every decision

edge_cases.description: An author re-skins a copy and claims transformational creativity though no defining constraint was actually altered.
edge_cases.trigger: claimed transformation with no constraint of the space changed
edge_cases.mitigation: require a named altered constraint for transformational claims; otherwise treat as copy plus cosmetic change

workflow.description: Establish the brief's originality bar as novel AND appropriate before any generation or scoring.
workflow.gate: both novelty and appropriateness criteria are explicit

workflow.description: Enumerate every source the output draws on and tag each source's role.
workflow.gate: an explicit (possibly empty, justified) source list exists

workflow.description: Generate novelty by recombining known elements and exploring the style space, capping per-element dominance.
workflow.gate: output recombines >=2 elements with no single dominant source element

workflow.description: Modify the source material and add at least one named own element so the output departs measurably from every source.
workflow.gate: measurable departure on structure and expression plus a named added element

workflow.description: Classify each borrow as reusable idea/style or protectable expression, and label pastiche versus parody.
workflow.gate: every borrow classified by layer with rationale

workflow.description: Compute source-distance and prior-output-distance and combine into an appropriateness-gated novelty score.
workflow.gate: score exposes its source, prior, and appropriateness sub-terms

workflow.description: Apply reuse cooldowns and freshness decay so devices are retired or refreshed before fatigue.
workflow.gate: each device has a cooldown and a freshness estimate

workflow.description: Probe for below-threshold overlap with protectable sources and surface the exact spans as evidence.
workflow.gate: all low-distance spans surfaced with source and distance

workflow.description: Record a per-borrow attribution ledger entry naming source, layer, and borrowed element.
workflow.gate: every material borrow has a ledger entry

workflow.description: Raise a derivative-risk flag on near-copies, explicitly stating transformation is not a safe harbor and the output is not cleared.
workflow.gate: flag asserts non-clearance and need for legal screening, never legal sufficiency

workflow.description: Route every flag with full provenance to compliance_heavy and block finalization until a determination returns.
workflow.gate: flagged output blocked until compliance_heavy returns a determination

workflow.description: Record the full provenance of the novelty and derivative-risk decision for reconstructability.
workflow.gate: decision reconstructable from inventory, distances, transforms, flags, and routing

priority_rationale: ORIGINALITY_DEFINITION, SOURCE_INVENTORY, and the three creativity modes are foundational; TRANSFORM_NOT_COPY and ADD_OWN_ELEMENT are the core levers; SOURCE_DISTANCE/PRIOR_OUTPUT_DISTANCE/NOVELTY_SCORE quantify novelty; SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE/DERIVATIVE_RISK_FLAG/COMPLIANCE_ROUTING and the audit trail close the method by flagging and routing derivative risk without deciding legal sufficiency.

dominance_rules.rule: DERIVATIVE_RISK_FLAG must fire on low source-distance regardless of how much transformation was applied
dominance_rules.rationale: transformation is a creative lever, not a legal safe harbor; modification cannot clear a near-copy
dominance_rules.trigger: a below-threshold output is treated as cleared because it was transformed
dominance_rules.action: raise the flag and block clearance; transformation never suppresses the flag

dominance_rules.rule: COMPLIANCE_ROUTING owns every legal-sufficiency determination; this KB never decides fair use, substantial similarity, or licensing
dominance_rules.rationale: legal sufficiency is out of scope (FP6/KU8) and belongs to compliance_heavy
dominance_rules.trigger: a legal-sufficiency call is attempted within this KB
dominance_rules.action: block and route the decision to compliance_heavy with full provenance

dominance_rules.rule: NOVELTY_SCORE must be gated by the brief's appropriateness operating point before it is reported
dominance_rules.rationale: a novel but off-brief output is not original under the standard definition
dominance_rules.trigger: novelty reported without an appropriateness gate
dominance_rules.action: apply the appropriateness gate from NOVELTY_APPROPRIATENESS_BALANCE

dominance_rules.rule: SOURCE_INVENTORY must exist before SOURCE_DISTANCE or SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE run
dominance_rules.rationale: distance and near-copy checks are only as complete as the source list
dominance_rules.trigger: distance computed against an empty or stale inventory
dominance_rules.action: block distance/probe until the inventory is current

dominance_rules.rule: TRANSFORM_NOT_COPY must produce a named added element verified absent from every source
dominance_rules.rationale: an unnamed or borrowed 'own element' does not convert borrowing into authorship
dominance_rules.trigger: a transform claim with no verified added element
dominance_rules.action: reject the transform claim until a genuine own element is present

dominance_rules.rule: COMBINATIONAL_CREATIVITY must cap per-element dominance and probe each recombined element
dominance_rules.rationale: a combination dominated by one protectable element is a near-copy of that element
dominance_rules.trigger: a single element exceeds the dominance threshold
dominance_rules.action: flag the dominant element via SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE

dominance_rules.rule: Declared brand signatures are exempt from REPETITION_GUARD cooldown but still subject to FRESHNESS_DECAY
dominance_rules.rationale: signature motifs build recognition and must not be mistaken for staleness
dominance_rules.trigger: a declared signature blocked as repetition
dominance_rules.action: exempt the signature from cooldown while tracking its freshness

dominance_rules.rule: SOURCE_ATTRIBUTION credit must never be treated as permission or clearance
dominance_rules.rationale: crediting a source does not authorize reproducing its protectable expression
dominance_rules.action: route the attributed near-copy to compliance regardless of credit

dominance_rules.rule: NOVELTY_AUDIT_TRAIL must record any flagged decision before finalization
dominance_rules.rationale: a flagged decision must be reconstructable for compliance and review
dominance_rules.trigger: finalization requested for a flagged output with no trail
dominance_rules.action: block finalization until the audit trail is recorded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not infer legal safe-harbor from transformation; modifying a copy does not clear it and rebuilding clearance later is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a near-copy as 'transformed therefore safe' and recalling it after a takedown

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not compute distances or probe near-copies against an incomplete source inventory; re-running after a missed source wastes the whole pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-scoring novelty after an uninventoried source surfaces in review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report a novelty score without the appropriateness gate; an off-brief 'novel' output must be redone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking an off-brief output that scored high on raw novelty

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not claim a new combination when one protectable element dominates; the near-copy must be fixed at the element level
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking a 'recombination' that was really a copy of one dominant element

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not treat attribution as permission; an attributed borrow can still require licensing or removal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: removing or relicensing attributed-but-uncleared material after publication

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not overuse a device past its cooldown and decay threshold; fatigue is expensive to recover from
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding audience engagement after a format is run into the ground

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip provenance on a flagged decision; retrofitting an audit trail requires re-running the whole assessment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-assessing a flagged output that could not be reconstructed for compliance

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not bypass compliance routing under deadline; an unscreened flagged output creates downstream legal rework
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-publication legal remediation of an unscreened flagged output

iteration_protocol.trigger: an output shipped on a 'transformed therefore safe' inference
iteration_protocol.action: reaffirm that transformation never clears risk in DERIVATIVE_RISK_FLAG and verify the COMPLIANCE_ROUTING block is enforced

iteration_protocol.trigger: a near-copy passed because its source was not inventoried
iteration_protocol.action: widen SOURCE_INVENTORY source classes and recompute SOURCE_DISTANCE and the SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a 'recombination' turned out to be dominated by one protectable element
iteration_protocol.action: lower the per-element dominance cap in COMBINATIONAL_CREATIVITY and probe each element
recalibrate the appropriateness gate in NOVELTY_APPROPRIATENESS_BALANCE and re-gate NOVELTY_SCORE

iteration_protocol.trigger: a paraphrase copied expression yet evaded the probe
iteration_protocol.action: add an expressive-distance axis in SOURCE_DISTANCE and retune the SUBSTANTIAL_SIMILARITY_PROBE threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format flopped from audience fatigue
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the decay model in FRESHNESS_DECAY and tighten the cooldown in REPETITION_GUARD

iteration_protocol.trigger: an attributed borrow was assumed cleared
iteration_protocol.action: reinforce the attribution-is-not-permission rule and route attributed near-copies through COMPLIANCE_ROUTING

iteration_protocol.trigger: a flagged decision could not be reconstructed
iteration_protocol.action: extend the NOVELTY_AUDIT_TRAIL schema and enforce trail-before-finalization

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
